title: core runs git in English, so its error text can be read on any machine
description:
Three places in core read git's stderr as English: packages/core/src/sync.ts:596 (`fetchBoard`, `/couldn't find remote ref/`), packages/core/src/sync.ts:624 (the push-rejected regex `non-fast-forward|fetch first|rejected|...`) and packages/core/src/digest.ts:111 (the same missing-ref check). On a machine whose locale is not English — this Mac speaks Turkish, git says `onulmaz: refs/heads/sober/board uzak başvurusu bulunamadı` — none of them match. `fetchBoard` then reads the ordinary first sync as an unreachable remote and refuses with 'origin could not be reached', and `pnpm integration` is red on 137 tests (every sync path: board, conflict, wire, cli, sync, team, digest, distribute, client, dashboard, three in mcp). CI is green only because the runners are English.

Every git call in core goes through one `exec` in packages/core/src/git.ts (line ~44; `git`, `gitWithEnv`, `gitVerbatim` all land there). Fix it once, there: spawn git with `LC_ALL: 'C'` placed after `...process.env` and before the caller's `...env`, so the user's locale never reaches git and a caller can still override. That pins every message the three regexes read; the regexes themselves do not change. Add one test in packages/core/src/git.test.ts (or next to the existing git tests) that sets `LANG`/`LC_ALL` to a non-English locale in `process.env` for the call, runs a fetch of a missing ref on a local bare remote, and asserts the error text contains `couldn't find remote ref` — the assertion that fails today on a Turkish machine. Do not touch the sync or digest regexes and do not add a per-call env at any call site: the point is that no future git call can forget it.

brief.approach:
Every git call in core goes through `exec` in packages/core/src/git.ts (line ~44): `git`, `gitWithEnv` and `gitVerbatim` all land there, and it spawns git with `env: { ...process.env, ...env }`. Three callers read git's stderr as English — `fetchBoard` in packages/core/src/sync.ts:596 (`/couldn't find remote ref/`), the push-rejected check in sync.ts:624 (`/non-fast-forward|fetch first|rejected|cannot lock ref|stale info/`) and packages/core/src/digest.ts:111 (the missing-ref check again). On this Mac git speaks Turkish (`onulmaz: refs/heads/sober/board uzak başvurusu bulunamadı`), none of them match, the first sync reads as an unreachable remote, and `pnpm integration` is red on 137 tests. `LC_ALL=C pnpm integration` is 375/375 green, which is the whole proof.

1. In `exec` in packages/core/src/git.ts, change the env to `{ ...process.env, LC_ALL: 'C', ...env }`: after `process.env` so the user's locale never reaches git, before the caller's `env` so a caller can still override. One line. Add a two-line comment above it naming why: three call sites match git's English text, and a pinned locale is what makes that a contract rather than luck. Do not touch the regexes in sync.ts or digest.ts, and do not add LC_ALL at any call site.

2. In packages/core/src/git.test.ts add one test next to the existing one, using `tmpRoot` from ./tmp.fixture.js: init a bare repository and a working repository with `git init`, `git remote add origin <bare>`, then call `git(work, 'fetch', 'origin', '+refs/heads/sober/board:refs/remotes/origin/sober/board')` with `process.env.LANG` and `process.env.LC_ALL` set to `tr_TR.UTF-8` for the duration of the call (save and restore in a try/finally). Expect it to reject with a `GitError` whose `stderr` contains `couldn't find remote ref`. That is the assertion that fails on a Turkish machine today and passes trivially on an English one — it pins the message the three regexes depend on.

3. Run `LANG=tr_TR.UTF-8 pnpm integration` at the end: with the pin in place the suite must be green under a Turkish locale, and that is the criterion that would have caught this on day one.

acceptance.proves: The new test passes: a fetch of a missing ref under a Turkish locale still reports `couldn't find remote ref`, so the error text core reads is pinned to English.
Exactly one hit, in git.ts's `exec` — the pin is in the one place every git call passes through, not at call sites.
The whole integration suite is green under a Turkish locale — the 137 sync-path failures on this machine are gone.
